items.title: Johnny St. Cyr Interview, 1958-08-27
items.q: I've experienced it with Charlie Cook's band.

ctx.x: A friend and I were talking the other day, it looks like the New Orleans fellows are about the only ones that can always pick the right tempo, it seems. I mean, they always know just whether-

Well, that they had. See, they, they, they, the fact that they were outlaw made them good. Because you'll find, I've experienced it with Charlie Cook's band. Charlie Cook has put numbers out for rehearsal. And the guys didn't like the number when they played it over the first time. And they made such a poor effort in playing the number that Charlie got disgusted and he put the number aside. He said, oh, we'll put this aside. Maybe later on we'll play it later. And maybe about three nights after, some guy come…
Man, you should, yeah, man, that number's good. You know what I mean? Well, those things.
